lines.english: "That's all for homeroom. I'm going on a business trip tomorrow, so Takahashi-sensei will be taking care of you all."
And so came January.
The first three days of the new year flew by in the blink of an eye, and soon enough, the third term started. These days, however, I've found myself just leisurely coasting along.
"Haruki!"
Some of my classmates are going as far as spending recess studying for their university entrance exams.
Others, perhaps preparing for job interviews, are barely even showing up in the classroom during the new term.
"Hey, Haruki."
"Hm?"
Meanwhile, most of the noisier people around are among those who have already been accepted to Houjou University via recommendation and are simply waiting for graduation.
And although I wouldn't say I'm as noisy as they are, I, too, have fully joined them in the endeavor of idly watching the days go by.
"Shouldn't you wake her up? Classes are over for today."
"What are you asking me for? She's right behind you, isn't she?"
"That's… true, but… Hey, Touma, wake up. Hey!"
And then there's…
A certain someone who has neither a recommendation nor any plans for the future.
My neighbor, who at this point is only waiting for graduation, has returned to being a sleeping prodigy just like she was in the past.
"Homeroom is over… Touma, your activity time has started."
"Fuaah… Mmm, okay. Thanks, Hayasaka."
"Ah… No worries."
"See ya!"
A time of bliss had begun for the entire school, except for those who willingly entered the hell of studying for university entrance exams.

The awkward atmosphere before the school festival and the excited atmosphere immediately after the festival ended is no longer here. It's a life where students come to school in the morning as usual, pass the day here, and return home in the evening.
"…What's going on with you two? You guys have been weird since the new year, no?"
"I already told you that it's nothing."
Except for this one guy who keeps intruding on others' feelings despite knowing nothing whatsoever.
"Well, you know, usually, whenever she leaves the classroom, you stare at her ass as if you're imagining licking her all over…"
"Not only do you sound vulgar, that's also utterly wrong. I could sue you for slander and win for sure."
"Touma too, you know. Whenever you give up and look away for a bit, she usually steals a glance at you…"
"…You're imagining things."
Once again… it's already January.
The time we spent together during the New Year's holidays feels like it was a long time ago, and has since vanished from my memory.
Because that's exactly what I… and another person… were hoping for.
"She's really going at it…"
"Yeah… She's trying her best."
"Okay then, let's jump in on the count of three, Haruki-kun."
"One, two, thr…"
"Let's not."
"Eh? Wha… hey…"
Before Setsuna touches the handle of Music Room 2, I grab her wrist and drag her down the hallway.
A small bag filled with snacks still hanging from her hand…
"I think we should… avoid meeting with Touma for a while."
"How come? Kazusa's been coming to school regularly too."
"That's because…"
"I want to be alone with you right now, Setsuna."
"I don't want to bother her until the competition is over. I mean, Touma finally went back to seriously playing the piano after all."
"Haruki-kun…"
There's no way I can reveal such a "motive."
If I did, Setsuna would be surprised, embarrassed, and then be happy… only to feel sad in the end.
"The competition is around the end of this month, right? So that's only about ten days from now."
We stopped by a cafe on our way back from school.
With how close we are now, we can spend some time alone here just by saying, "Let's stop by."
On top of that…
"Ah…"
"Okay, Setsuna? Can we do that?"
"H-Haruki-kun…"
"What?"
"There are other students from our school here. See? Those girls over there are staring at us…"
"Is there something wrong with that?"
"…Nope."
Setsuna places her right hand on my own right hand that's already holding her left.
With how close we are now, we can do things like this unabashedly.
"Speaking of which, Kazusa is taking private piano lessons every day now. She told me about it when I was on the phone with her the other night."
"Setsuna, you… aren't you worried about your phone bills?"
She chats with me for well over an hour daily too.
"What's more, it seems that the teacher is a famous music university professor, even taking a break from lectures to give Touma one-on-one lessons…"
"As expected of the Touma family… They really have some crazy connections."
"And it seems that the teacher is a guy."
"Ah, really now…"
"…Does it bother you?"
"Of course it bothers me."
"Eh, really?"
"I hope that he's not overly strict. I hope he will let Touma hang out with us every once in a while."
The model answer that I had already prepared inside my head smoothly flows out of my mouth.
I had been running various simulations inside my head so that I could answer without hesitation in case questions like this one came up.
"What's the matter? Did I say something strange?"
"No… She said that the teacher is actually over 50 years old."
"Ah, I see."
She must have withheld that information until the end on purpose.
Is she teasing me, trying to read me, or perhaps worrying about me, or maybe even all of that…?
"Anyway, we'll be able to meet at the competition, so we all just need to be patient for a while."
"Ah, yeah."
No matter what Setsuna's intentions were, I just need to make sure not to lose my way.
"In turn, let's cheer for her at the competition with all we've got until our voices crack."
"I'm pretty sure that it's against proper manners to do that at a piano competition…"
From now on, I'll try to avoid Touma as much as possible.
"Then, after the competition is over, let's hang out again, all three of us. Speaking of which, your birthday is next month, right Setsuna?"
"Hm? Yeah, that's right. February 14th."
"…That's a convenient day to exchange presents."
Until I can truly think of Touma as nothing more than a good friend.
"Should we meet up at my house on the 14th, then? I'll make a lot of delicious food!"
"You should let others treat you for once, it's your birthday…"
Until there aren't any awkward pauses or emotional tension between us.
Until I can brag about Setsuna with a smile.
Until she can accept my bragging with a smile and make fun of it.
"In that case, you'll have to keep me company until then, okay? Don't let me feel lonely, okay?"
I'm sure that such a day will come soon enough.
"I promise… I'll never leave you alone, Setsuna."
If Setsuna and I cross all the lines.
…If we become one in both body and soul.
From the next day on… Touma stopped coming to school.
According to Setsuna's texts, she's started practicing sixteen hours a day and can't take a single step outside of her house.
So I'm…
I'm thankful to Touma for avoiding me like this.
"…As if I'd be able to hear from here."
…Even so.
I'm so fickle and weak-willed, my words and actions are in clear contradiction… I'm as good as a stalker by now.
The front entrance lights are on. They're on inside as well.
But there are no signs of life at all, meaning that it's pointless for me to be here.
"…Let's just leave."
I had hoped that I would be able to hear the sound of the piano. I had hoped that I would see her shadow through the window, at least.
…Even though I already knew that her practice room is in the basement, completely soundproof.
I didn't expect that I would give up after only three days of not seeing her face, but I got off the train midway without realizing it.
This is all because I had to take care of a bunch of favors for other people, so I didn't leave the school until 8 o'clock.
…Our nightly practice used to start at the same time in the past.
"Ah…"
"You stalker."
That's what the text says…
It came 30 minutes after I left her house, as if she was calculating when I would get home.
"Do your best."
I send a reply titled "From Stalker."
"I'm going to become someone unreachable to you."
And the title says "I'm going to win."
"…Do your best."
"Hey, um… How many more are there?"
"This is number 18, so she's up next."
"Ehh? It's already her turn…?"
"You've been asking me after every single person for a while now…"
And so… came February.
First Sunday of the month. We'll finally get to see Touma's true colors today.
The finals of the competition.
"Will Kazusa be okay… Did she have a proper breakfast?"
"…Knowing her, even if she ate something, it'd probably be CalorieMate or some jelly."
"That's not good! You need to eat something filling to have enough stamina…"
"…Calm down already, Setsuna. It's not like you're the one playing."
"I-I'm feeling nervous precisely because I'm not the one playing."
"Even though you were shaking in your boots when you first sang?"
"…You're such a bully, Haruki-kun."
Setsuna has been chattering away about Touma's horoscope, the amount of brushstrokes in her name, and other various fortunes for today up until just a moment ago.
When I told her, "Those are just superstitions," she proceeded to panic about how she forgot to give Touma a good luck charm.
She finally quieted down after being warned by the staff, but now she's going on about breakfast.
"Touma will be fine. She's a lot braver than we are."
She used to sweep all junior competitions, after all, earning her the title of a genius child of a genius.
"I would've been prepared for this if she'd called us for the preliminaries. She didn't even tell me her preliminary schedules."
"She must have not wanted us to see her if she failed in the preliminaries. I guess even Touma wasn't all that confident this time around."
…That said, I actually knew the preliminaries' schedules.
I thoroughly combed over the event host's website and looked up all the schedules regarding the piano competition.
"I heard that over a hundred people entered the preliminaries. After the second round, there were only twenty people left."
"When we found out, Touma was already among those top twenty… She's amazing."
But I didn't tell Setsuna about the schedule. She definitely would've said, "Let's go cheer for her!" if I had.
Even though it was on a weekday. During school hours, no less.
…Besides, I didn't have the courage to go.
"This is… not a students' competition, right? Every contestant here is an adult, and really good at that."
"The entry age limit is between 18 to 30 years of age."
Meaning that Touma is the youngest participant…
"I wonder if she would receive a university recommendation if she won this?"

She's suddenly decided to participate in such a tough competition as a means to test her skills after two years of being absent from the field, and I can't say whether such a decision is typical of her, or something else…
"It would be nice if it were a nearby university. Hey, what was the name of that music university that's close by? The one that the music students from our school often end up going to…"
"Don't get ahead of yourself yet, Setsuna. Let's just be glad that she's made it into the finals for now."
"Aww, Haruki-kun, you're such a spoilsport. Kazusa hasn't even played yet…"
"Next is number 19, Touma Kazusa-san."
"She's here! There she is, Haruki-kun!"
"I said calm down…"
While I pretend to calm Setsuna down, my eyes are locked on the stage.
Wearing a chic black dress and with her long, sleek black hair swaying behind her, Kazusa confidently enters the stage.
"That's her, that's Touma Youko's daughter. She's been the talk of the competition since the preliminaries. She's the youngest competitor this year."
"Heh… Like mother, like daughter, I guess. Or maybe she's just an elite who's received special education since childhood."
…Except, she'd been rebelling against her mother until recently.
Setsuna tightly grips my hand.
All at once, I can sense her heartbeat and sweat on her palm, as well as her body tensing up nervously.
"Setsuna…"
I hold Setsuna's nervous hand and sigh lightly while falling into an altogether different train of thought.
Such as… "Will she find me in this crowd like she promised she would?"
Such as… "Black outfits suit her, after all. In fact, she looks good in whatever she wears."
"…Haruki-kun."
"Setsuna, I said calm down…"
"My hand… it hurts."
I'm such an idiot.
"…Sorry. To tell you the truth, I'm really nervous."
"Then… let's listen to it together, all tense and nervous like this, okay?"
"Okay…"
Setsuna takes my hand once again. This time, she entwines her fingers with mine so that our hands don't come apart.
In turn, I firmly grasp Setsuna's hand, and we sense each other's heartbeat through our nervously sweaty palms.
And then…
Finally, Touma's performance begins.
To be honest…
Setsuna and I most likely don't understand even a portion of the true worth of this performance unfolding before us.
We can only understand the simple things, like her blistering pace, the force at which she strikes each key, and her accurate sense of rhythm.
And judging these performances based on the above criteria, all eighteen performers until now sounded nearly perfect. Untrained ears like ours really can't tell which is better than the other.
Critics would use terms like "vibrant sound," or "rich expressiveness"… Such termsーwhich are vibrant and richly expressive in their own rightーwould sound wrong if amateurs like us used them.
Even so, we hold each other's hands tightly to the point where our nails are digging into our skin, as the overwhelming stream of music continues to engulf us.
We probably can't help but have a sense of natural bias because it's our friend who's playing.
However, still…
Touma's piano playing was enough to completely throw us into shock.
When it comes down to it, I really can't give up on being Touma's fan yet.
By the time we finally let go of each other's hands to applaud, my eyes that were completely fixed on the stage… had become embarrassingly swollen and red.
"Fifth place. Number 8, Koyama Shiori-san."
"Uu… Uh…"
"…Have you calmed down a bit?"
"Y-Yeah… Haah…!"
…Thankfully, because the person next to me was in an even worse state, my own distress went unnoticed.
The handkerchief I took out to use myself after Touma's song ended was completely monopolized by Setsuna.
"That was amazing…"
"Yeah…"
"There really are things that you can feel are amazing even if you don't understand them well…"
"Yeah…"
"Fourth place. Number 15, Takahashi Shingo-san."
Although the genre was completely different…
I feel like Touma proved on her own here that our performance during the school festival was merely child's play.
"She'll definitely win a place, right? She worked so hard after all."
Effort is not a criterion in judging competition performances.
Not to mention, if each participant's efforts until today were taken into account, Touma might actually lose the most points out of everyone.
However…
"I hope she wins."
Touma's performance more than lived up to our expectations.
At the very least, her performance was by no means inferior to the others'. An amateur like me couldn't really tell any difference.
"Third place. Number 1, Araki Yoshikaze-san."
"She's definitely in the running. She was a cut above the rest, after all."
"Yeah."
Because I realize that I can't judge this calmly and without bias, my response gets stuck in my throat.
Even so, I try my best to calm down…
"Could she be second? Or maybe first? Since she's come this far, it'd be great if she got first…"
"…Yeah."
At this point in time, I can't help but get swept up by the same prediction Setsuna's made.
But that's only natural… Touma really did put on an amazing performance.
On top of that, a cynic like her who never dreams went as far as promising me that she will win.
"Second place. Number 17, Itou Michiko-san."
"…!? Haruki-kun…"
Before Setsuna's hand repositions in my hand, I tightly grasp it.
…I realize it's a long shot.
Being the youngest participant, not having received any lessons for two years… If you think about it rationally, it's a miracle that she's even made it to the finals.
But she's already made one miracle happen. It wouldn't be surprising if she pulled off another one now.
Only first place remains.
It's the place Touma naturally always took until middle school.
If there's ever been an opportunity for Touma to single-handedly make up for the worst three years of her life, it's this…
"And the first place goes to…"
"I'll have cafe au lait."
"Okay, I'll have the blend then."
"Uuh… uu…!"
"…Two of them, please."
"One cafe au lait and two blends. Coming right up."
"Uu… uu…"
"…Do something, would you? She's your girlfriend, isn't she?"
"You're the one she's crying about. You do something about it."
"I-I'm sorry. I'll stop soon… Haa…"
"Come on, your hopes were up in the clouds. What kind of joke were you making when you said that there's no way I wouldn't get first place?"
"That's… well…"
First place. Number 12, Hashimoto Kenji-san.
And with that, I hereby close the announcement of the results.
…As the announcer's words echoed throughout the hall, we stood there dumbfounded, surrounded by thunderous applause.
"I knew from the preliminaries that it would come down to number 12. He was on a totally different level all by himself. I almost felt like a fool having stood on the same stage as him."
"…I didn't think your performance was any worse than his, Touma."
Actually, to be honest, I don't even remember how number 12's performance sounded.
"Well, your ears wouldn't be able to tell, sure. Honestly, even a novice should be able to tell the difference pretty easily, but…"
"Well, excuse me for being an amateur with less than one year of experience with the guitar…"
"That guy will definitely be getting his big break soon… Well, not that it's much coming from a loser."
With all said and done, I hugged Setsuna, who was crying after the announcement, and we waited awkwardly outside the waiting room.
Eventually, Touma met us with a noticeably cool expression.
"So cheer up already, Setsuna. Then again, I can't say it's not flattering to see you so depressed like this."
"It was amazing… It was really amazing, Kazusa. And that just makes it even more frustrating…"
"Setsuna really is such a nice girl. She's too good for you, Kitahara."
"Don't badmouth someone to compliment another person."
Not to mention it's annoying to have you pointing out things I'm well aware of.
"It doesn't bother me. I'm actually thinking that it's good that I didn't place."
As Setsuna rubs her eyes, Touma reaches across the table and starts sincerely and gently stroking her hair.
…The fact that it looks terribly similar to what I usually do with Setsuna likely means that anyone would want to do that to her once.
"How come? Even though you tried so hard… you weren't rewarded…"
"If you ask me why…
Aah, well… I'm completely hopeless!"
"…You don't sound like it's not bothering you in the least, though."
"No, I'm not talking about not placing. What I mean is, I… it doesn't feel right for me to be this relieved."
"I don't get it."
"Never knowing when to let things go, always brooding on the past… and having such a grim personality that just won't let me move on…"
"…Let's forget I said anything just now."
"I really have no idea what you're talking about."
What confuses me the most is Touma putting her head down and self-deprecatingly talking about herself like this, something I've never seen her do before.
Then, still acting so unlike her usual self, Touma looks up at me and gives me a look of sincere relief with a shy smile.
"Well, whatever. There's always next time. I can just try again, so I'm not all that disappointed."
"You'll try your best again?"
"I've realized that I have talent in piano. After all, making the finals after messing around for two years must be proof that I'm a genius."
"It doesn't come close to your talent in bragging about yourself, though."
"Also…"
"Oww!"
"It was fun, after all… Impressing someone with my music."
"It's cold…"
"I wouldn't be surprised if it started snowing."
We held an impromptu consolation party together in a family restaurant until it was late at night.
When we finally decided to call it a day and came out, we were met by a dark sky and chilly winds.
"All right, I'm heading this way. Kitahara, take care of Setsuna… Please keep her safe from those evil hands of yours, okay?"
"How am I supposed to…"
In this cold air, chilly enough to freeze both body and soul, Touma was entirely like her regular self.
"Hey, Kazusa?"
"Hm?"
"Will you be coming to school again from tomorrow on?"
"I guess I will… since I don't have a good reason to skip anymore."
As she says that, she brings both of her hands to her lips and lets out a white puff of breath through them.
"That's great… That means the three of us will be together again starting tomorrow."
"If that's what you want, Setsuna."
Through her demeanor and speech, along with the lonely atmosphere she's brought about recently, Touma looks like she's drawing a line…
"Yeah, thanks. Let's get along until graduation, Kazusa."
"…There, you heard her. I hope we'll get along until graduation, Kitahara."
"…Yeah. Likewise."
"Don't ignore me like you did last month. It was pretty hard on me too, okay?"
That's why…
Even the ambiguity in her behavior, where I can't tell if she's being serious or merely teasing me, feels pleasant in comparison.
"See you later, then!"
"See you tomorrow!"
"Ah, yeah…"
This new side of her is enough to throw me off balance once more.
Is she cutting us off again? Was I wrong in thinking that she had opened up to begin with?
I can't read that girl. I've known that all along… but she's too much for me to handle.
"Hey, it's me. Yeah, it's over. Now? I had dinner and now I'm on my way home."
"And about the results… Yeah, turns out the two-year gap was too much, after all."
"It was not good at all. Just like you said. I still have a long way to go."
"Well, nothing we can do now. It's all my fault. I'm not sure if it's too late to start now, but I'll work hard for another year, and then next year I'll… Huh?"
"…You were… there?"
"Huh?"
"W-Wait… hold on… I… I failed, you know? I didn't live up to your expectations, right?"
"So what do you… what do you mean?"
"What do you mean, I passed…?"
